text: Designing a good API is like creating a map for other programmers. A well-built REST API uses clear, logical endpoints—for example, `/users` to get a list of users or `/users/123` to update one user. Always return meaningful status codes, such as `200 OK` for success, `404 Not Found` for a missing resource, or `400 Bad Request` for invalid input. This helps users instantly know what happened. Equally important is documentation: explain each endpoint, its parameters, and expected responses with simple examples. Finally, never break your existing users. Use versioning, like `/v1/users`, so you can add new features without disrupting old code. A consistent, well-documented API saves everyone time and frustration.
